_about: The club's own facts, in one file a non-developer can edit from a phone. Everything the site asserts about the club is read from here (src/lib/content.ts); a fact that is not settled is a slot with `value: null` and the bracketed text that is waiting for a source, so the absence is explicit rather than invented. Rules this file answers to: DESIGN.md 'Copy' (state the fact, name where it came from, give a path out, carry the date; never state a frequency without a source; `[BRACKETS]` stay bracketed until a source exists), D92, D136 (no fabricated numbers), record 0010 (missing content is a designed state, never a blank and never a build failure).
_override: For a preview or a review build, copy src/content.local.example.json to src/content.local/<name>.json (gitignored, like .dev.vars) - it deep-merges over this file. Nothing tracked can turn a placeholder on: `scripts/check-content.mjs` fails any build that contains one, so a review-only state cannot reach the apex.
_sources: A claim may carry its source once, on the object that holds the group, and every claim under it inherits that source - `unsourcedSlots` in src/lib/content.ts and scripts/check-content.mjs walk ancestors, so 'the operator listed these on 2026-11-03' is written once rather than pasted nine times.

cadence.source: the operator's vision letter of 2026-11-19, docs/the-authors-vision-2026-11-19.md §3: 'Cadence is twice monthly.' Supersedes the ruling of 2026-10-31 ('Monthly is more generally correct; actual rhythm is ~every other week, occasionally skipped', recorded in .notes/roadmap-events.md), which is kept here because the older word is what the artifact used to claim. Corroborated, not derived: the organiser's own row titles in data/events.json say 'Bimonthly Social', and series.config.mjs holds two 14-day series (D175).
cadence.correction: docs/the-authors-vision-2026-11-19.md §3 - the operator corrects this word by editing this value; the row stays to record what was shipped and when
cadence.note: DESIGN.md forbids a frequency word with no source ('join us every week' survived two years - D92). This one has a named source, which is what keeps the slot legal. **No built page paints it**: the shipped rhythm sentence is generated from the rows the calendar publishes (src/lib/rhythm.mjs, D383), and `grep -rl cadence dist/client/` reads no hits @measured 2026-11-19. Two things a future round must not do quietly: (1) put a frequency word on a page without adding that exact phrase to src/lib/cadence.mjs, which is the list `check:content` fails on - the list carries 'twice a month' and 'bimonthly' but not 'twice monthly', so the author's words as typed would reach a page unchecked; (2) state a frequency at all without deciding that the generated weekday sentence is not the better answer, since a typed word is a claim the rows can disprove (D189: the source cannot confirm a rhythm). Set value to null and the copy falls back to naming the paths out instead of claiming a rhythm.

focus.placeholder: [what the club is taking up right now, if it wants to name one]
focus.note: Emptied 2026-11-03 on the operator's word: 'We no longer have that focus. We have no current focus at all right now.' The value it held ('Number Theory and Abstract Algebra') was pre-existing site copy with no source - `check:content` had it listed as an unsourced claim - so there was nothing to correct it against. What the club is actually pulling on is in `threads`, which is deliberately undated (see `threads._rule`). The hero renders nothing when this slot is empty rather than inventing a subject. The date-bearing label lane that used to sit under the hero is gone (D239, 2026-11-07) - the hero prints a fixed locator that cannot go stale, and the zero-event signal now lives on the schedule band, which is the surface that actually draws a calendar.

threads.source: operator, 2026-11-03, describing what the club has been discussing in its Discord channel: 'IBM Qiskit quantum computing tools, theoretical quantum physics, proof assistant languages like Lean, news in the general math field, LLMs affects on the math field, favorite math-related Youtube content, foundations of mathematics, considering the implications of arithmetic with slight changes, math exercises/puzzles that don't require expertise in a field and have interesting solutions'
threads._rule: Undated, untitled and not an archive, on purpose. Operator ruling, 2026-11-03: 'I don't want the home page to give anyone an idea that our groups interests are as narrow as what we have done historically, so I don't want to name enough specific things to give enough information to allow a pattern to emerge.' So this list carries no dates, no sequence, no book titles, no authors and no run of past topics a reader could extrapolate from. A thread that goes quiet is edited out rather than left as a record, and nothing here implies the club did something in the past or will do it in the future. Item strings are reworded for a newcomer (that is presentation, not a new claim); the operator's own words are the source above.

membership.value: The club's list of members is its Meetup group page
membership.source: the club's own Meetup group page, fetched 2026-11-03, whose member-count link reads '280 members' (https://www.meetup.com/minneapolis-mathematics-book-club/members/); the operator confirmed the figure and added that about ten of them are regular attendees
membership.note: The number is NOT painted (D276, 2026-11-11). Since D306 (2026-11-14) the page prints the sentence in `value` plus a provenance stamp derived from `asOf` (`provenanceStamp()`, e.g. "last read <n> days ago" inside 30 days, `on 3 Nov 2026` beyond it - D322) and never the calendar date: `/dates` is the only surface that prints a date (D306's rule; the route moved from `/schedule` under D373), and `check:dated-surfaces` refuses one on `/`. Keep `asOf` exactly as sourced - it is the input to that age. 280 stays here as the sourced figure behind the claim, and `scripts/check-rsvp-page.mjs` fails the build if a tally of people reaches the built HTML in prose or in an attribute (D265). History: the site used to render Math.floor(Math.random()*100+150)+'+ members' - a different community size on every request (D136, deleted); then it printed '280 on the Meetup list - counted Nov 3, 2026' in the join band, which is a headcount dressed as provenance. Do NOT publish the regular-attendee figure: ten is a fact about who shows up, it reads as a discouragement on a join page, and the operator's plan is to grow it by formalising special interest groups. Re-read the number when the page is next edited - a dated figure that has gone stale is the failure this slot's asOf exists to make visible.

The club has no attendance record in this tree, so the letter is the source and the sentence stays in this SLOT rather than moving into prose, because prose of the same sentence would fail the count rules (D421, D265)
turnout.correction: docs/reply-to-the-communication-review-round-8-2026-11-18.md §4 ledger C6 — the operator corrects this claim by editing this value; keep the sentence in the slot, since check:rsvp-page exempts a spelled-out count only inside a sourced slot
turnout.note: This is the site's first painted headcount, and D265's rule is that a headcount may reach a page only from a slot carrying a source and an asOf date. `scripts/check-rsvp-page.mjs` moved **three commits after** this sentence shipped - the sentence in `fe1bb9b`, the rule in `31aae87` (**D406**) @measured 2026-11-17 by `git log --format=%h -6 -- scripts/check-rsvp-page.mjs` and `git show 31aae87:scripts/check-rsvp-page.mjs` (2 `SPELL_RE` occurrences; `fe1bb9b` carries 0) - so for three commits a spelled headcount reached the page with no detector, and the reply doc's §9 records that breach rather than dressing it up (**D420**). Its `COUNT_RE` now catches spelled-out numbers as well as digits, and a match is exempted only when it sits inside the span of a value that this file sources. That is the whole invariant - a count of people on a page must be a grounded claim, not a leftover from a third-party snapshot (D136's random member count is the defect this rule was born from). DRAFT CLAIM: replace `value` with the operator's number and the gate needs no change.
